# slopball — next version

DERIVED by `make next-version` from .wire-changes/ and the last tag. Nothing
here ran: this tool never tags and never pushes, the same way
`make deploy-checklist` never runs wrangler. Cutting the release is yours.

  last tag       v0.1.0
  pending        nothing
  next version   v0.1.1
  why            the ledger is empty — the wire did not move, and a release
                 changes more than the wire, so the patch moves.

## The changelog

Nothing is appended to CHANGELOG.md: no entry was pending, so no sentence was
written by anybody who knew. The tag is the whole record of this release.

## The sequence

```sh
git add -A && git commit -m "release v0.1.1"
git tag -a v0.1.1 -m "v0.1.1"
git push origin main --follow-tags
```

The number is derived, not decided: it is max(class) over the pending entries,
and an empty ledger is a patch because a release changes more than the wire. It
is still a suggestion — tag something else if a release needs a number for a
reason the wire cannot see, and the next derivation reads whatever tag it finds.
